decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 50 basis points, to 3%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Richard W. Fisher.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 50 basis points to 3 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee has decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate 75 basis points to 3-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: Financial markets remain under considerable stress, and credit has tightened further for some businesses and households.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “While strains in short-term funding markets have eased somewhat, broader financial market conditions have continued to deteriorate and credit has tightened furt…”

changes.quote: Moreover, recent information indicates a deepening of the housing contraction as well as some softening in labor markets.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Moreover, incoming information indicates a deepening of the housing contraction as well as some softening in labor markets.”

changes.quote: The Committee took this action in view of a weakening of the economic outlook and increasing downside risks to growth.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Today’s policy action, combined with those taken earlier, should help to promote moderate growth over time and to mitigate the risks to economic activity.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: However, downside risks to growth remain.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Appreciable downside risks to growth remain.”

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 50 basis points to 3 percent.
Moreover, recent information indicates a deepening of the housing contraction as well as some softening in labor markets.
However, downside risks to growth remain.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.59% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.78% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.69% would rise by about $17.14 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 5%, and employers added an average of 99k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.1% over the past year (December 2007); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.1% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 59%, cut 35%, hike 5%.
